nodes.title: MODEL DOWNLOADS - read this first
widgets_values:
# Model downloads

Everything here is free. Put each file in the folder shown, then restart
ComfyUI. About **13 GB** in total.

---

## 1. The model that reads your picture

`ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/`

- [qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors) - 4.9 GB

> In the loader, **type must be `krea2`**. That is what gives it eyes. Any other
> setting and your prompts come back empty.

---

## 2. The model that draws - Z-Image Turbo

`ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/` - pick **one**:

| File | Size | Who it is for |
|---|---|---|
| [z_image_turbo_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/z_image_turbo/resolve/main/split_files/diffusion_models/z_image_turbo_bf16.safetensors) | 11.5 GB | works on any card |
| [z_image_turbo_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/z_image_turbo/resolve/main/split_files/diffusion_models/z_image_turbo_int8_convrot.safetensors) | 5.8 GB | smaller, faster |
| `z_image_turbo_nvfp4.safetensors` | 4.2 GB | **RTX 50-series only** - [same folder](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/z_image_turbo/tree/main/split_files/diffusion_models) |

The workflow arrives pointing at the nvfp4 file. **If you are not on a 50-series
card, open the Load Diffusion Model node and pick the one you downloaded.**

`ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/`

- [qwen_3_4b.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/z_image_turbo/resolve/main/split_files/text_encoders/qwen_3_4b.safetensors) - 7.5 GB

`ComfyUI/models/vae/`

- [ae.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/z_image_turbo/resolve/main/split_files/vae/ae.safetensors) - 0.3 GB

---

## 3. Tile ControlNet - holds your layout steady

`ComfyUI/models/model_patches/`

The workflow is set to the **Tile** model from Alibaba's Z-Image-Turbo-Fun
ControlNet family. Find it on the
[alibaba-pai page](https://huggingface.co/alibaba-pai) - look for
`Z-Image-Turbo-Fun-Controlnet-Tile`.

The **Union** model also works - just select it in the ModelPatchLoader node:

- [Z-Image-Turbo-Fun-Controlnet-Union.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/alibaba-pai/Z-Image-Turbo-Fun-Controlnet-Union/resolve/main/Z-Image-Turbo-Fun-Controlnet-Union.safetensors)

---

## 4. Optional - an ESRGAN enlarger

`ComfyUI/models/upscale_models/`

Only needed if you switch the Tile Planner to *AI upscaler model*. Any 4x model
from [OpenModelDB](https://openmodeldb.info/) will do. Out of the box the
workflow uses Lanczos and needs nothing here, so that loader ships
**unwired** - connect it to the planner's `upscale_model` input when you
want it.

---

## Where everything goes

```
ComfyUI/
└── models/
    ├── text_encoders/
    │   ├── qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors    <- reads your picture
    │   └── qwen_3_4b.safetensors                <- Z-Image text encoder
    ├── diffusion_models/
    │   └── z_image_turbo_*.safetensors          <- pick one
    ├── vae/
    │   └── ae.safetensors
    ├── model_patches/
    │   └── Z-Image-Turbo-Fun-Controlnet-Tile-*.safetensors
    └── upscale_models/
        └── (optional 4x model)
```

## Custom nodes you need

Install these three from the ComfyUI Manager:

- **ComfyUI-Smart-Upscaler** (this pack)
- **ComfyUI-KJNodes** - the Set/Get wires
- **rgthree-comfy** - the before/after sliders

nodes.title: Prompt Director - the only box you really touch
widgets_values:
This writes the master prompt, and every tile prompt comes from it.

**It is already filled in for this workflow** - there is nothing to load.

**Load Preset** (at the bottom) starts out empty. It fills up with add-on
preset packs you install, and with your own presets saved by the
**Save My Preset to Disk** button below it.

1. **Instructions** - the job. Edit freely; this is the whole recipe.
2. **Your request** - optional. Only fill this in if you want something *changed*, e.g. "make it night time". Leave blank for a plain upscale.
3. **Not in this image** - optional. If the model keeps seeing something that is not there, type it here and it is banned.
4. **Extra words** - added to the end of every tile prompt.
5. **How much detail** - more detail = better prompts, slower. *Adaptive* is a good middle. *Maximum* names everything.
6. **Delete colour names** - leave OFF. Only for the rare case where a model tints whole squares one flat shade.

nodes.title: START HERE
widgets_values:
# Smart Upscaler

Most upscalers look at one small square at a time, so they guess. A patch of
roof becomes "brown texture". This one **reads your whole picture first**, then
writes a separate, accurate prompt for every square before anything is redrawn.

## Run it in four steps

1. **Load your picture** in box 1. It arrives pointing at
   `Upscale_Test_Image.png` - copy that file from this pack's `workflow`
   folder into `ComfyUI/input/` first, or just pick a picture of your own.
2. **Nothing to set up in box 2.** The Prompt Director already carries
   the right instructions for this workflow. Leave it alone the first time.
3. **Nothing to set up in boxes 5 and 6 either.** The Tile Planner ships at
   2x; raise its **scale_factor** when you want bigger.
4. Press **Run**.

## When it finishes

- Box 6 has a **slider** to drag between the original and the result, and the
  saved file.
- Box 3 shows **the prompt written for every single tile**. If part of the
  picture came out wrong, read its prompt - that is almost always the reason.

## Taking longer than you expected?

Big scales make a lot of tiles. Check the **"Before you run"** box in box 2 -
it tells you how many tiles you are about to render before you commit.

Every step is cached. Running again only redoes what you changed.

**Model downloads are in the note to the right.** ->

nodes.title: What to change here
widgets_values:
### Your picture

Drop any photo in. Small, soft, or old pictures are exactly what this is for.

### The upscaler model above it

**Optional, and deliberately not wired up.** Out of the box the workflow uses
**Lanczos**, which needs no download at all.

To use an AI enlarger instead: download a 4x model, pick it in that loader,
drag its output into the Tile Planner's **upscale_model** input, and set the
planner's first dropdown to *AI upscaler model*.

nodes.title: Tile Planner - what the dials do
widgets_values:
**scale_factor** - how many times bigger. 2 = double. This is the one dial most people change. Bigger = more tiles = longer.

**min / max_tile_size** - how big each square is, in final pixels. Leave at 1024-1536. Lower them only if you run out of video memory.

**overlap / feather** - how much neighbouring squares share, so you cannot see the joins. If you spot seams, raise **overlap to 128** and **feather to 64** - on most pictures this costs no extra tiles at all.

**upscale_method** - Lanczos (honest) or an AI model (sharper, but invents detail early).

Everything else is fine as it is. Check the **"Before you run"** box below for how many tiles you are about to make.

nodes.title: Finishing dials
widgets_values:
### Colour match to the original

Fixes squares that came back slightly the wrong shade. One dropdown does it:
it ships on *Match source brightness*, which is right for a normal upscale.

Set it to **No colour change** if you asked for a look change (night, style),
otherwise it will drag your new look back to the old colours.

### Stitch the tiles back together

One dropdown here too. It ships on *Photo upscale, seams hidden* - the
setting for a picture that was already correct and just needs to be bigger.

Pick an **I changed the look** preset instead when you asked for a style, a
time of day, or a repair, so your new look is not pulled back to the original.

The five dials each preset writes live under **Advanced** on the node. You
only need them if a preset is close but not quite right.

### The two comparison sliders

Drag the divider to see before and after. The top one shows the plain
enlargement, so you can tell what the model actually added.

### Tile Inspector

Click any tile to see the exact prompt that made it.

nodes.title: Why you would use this
widgets_values:
**Skip it for a normal run.** Leave the dropdown on *All tiles*.

Switch to **One tile test** and pick a tile number to render just that one
square. Every prompt is still written and logged - only the drawing is limited.

Use it to try a different denoise or strength setting in seconds instead of
waiting for the whole picture.

Tile numbers are the T-numbers shown in the tile map and the prompt log.

nodes.title: How the picture gets enlarged
widgets_values:
How the picture is enlarged before the model touches it.

**Lanczos** (the default) just makes it bigger and keeps everything honest.
**AI upscaler model** can look sharper, but it invents small detail before the model ever sees it.

Try both on your own picture. Results are cached, so the second try is quick.

nodes.title: The four dials that change how it looks
widgets_values:
**denoise** (in KSampler, bottom dial) - how much freedom the model has.
Ships at `0.6`. `0.4` stays very close to your picture, `0.65` invents
more detail. Too high and it starts adding things that were never there.
**This is the main dial.**

**strength** (Tile ControlNet) - how tightly the layout is held. `0.6` is a good
middle. Higher = safer, flatter. Lower = more invention.

**steps** - 8 to 12 is plenty for a Turbo model. More is rarely better.

**shift** (Model Sampling) - fine tuning. Leave at 1.5 unless you know why.

**CFG** 1.0 to 1.5 A hack above 1.0 to fix the low denoise errors.
---

**Swapping models:** this whole green block is replaceable. Any model that takes
a picture and a prompt and returns a picture can go here - just feed the result
into `Set_Z-Turbo` and add it to the Generator switch.

Z-Turbo has this strange behavoir where it introduces "stick" like objects on lower denoise.

nodes.title: Before you run: output size, how many tiles, cache status
Reading the prompt log
widgets_values:
Every tile prompt this run produced, in order, plus the scene summary the
whole picture produced.

They are also written to disk:

```
ComfyUI/output/Smart-Upscaler/logs/
```

**This is the first place to look when something comes out wrong.** If tile 4
painted a bush where there should be a wall, its prompt will say "bush" - and
then you know it is a reading problem, not a model problem.

The purple box to the left shows the **scene summary**: what the whole picture
is, which large areas repeat across tiles, and what the main subject is.

nodes.title: Adding more models
widgets_values:
Only the selected generator actually runs - the others cost nothing.

To add one: build your model chain, end it with a `Set_` node, then drag a
matching `Get_` node into `generator_2` here. The dropdown renames itself
from the group title.

nodes.title: Do not change this loader setting
widgets_values:
Leave `type` set to **krea2**.

That setting is what makes this loader able to SEE your picture. Any other setting loads a text-only model, and your tile prompts come back empty.

nodes.title: Compare: original vs simply enlarged (no AI detail yet)

Prompt Director - the master prompt
widgets_values:
TASK: Upscale / Detailer

Rebuild this image at higher resolution with real, generated detail. Nothing moves and nothing is added:
the same content, colors, lighting, and layout come back, but every surface should return with true,
believable texture instead of soft, enlarged pixels.

Describe each area for what it IS. Name the thing, the material it is made of, its visible color, and how
that surface looks close up - grain, weave, roughness, wetness, and how its edges catch the light. The new
detail is generated from that description, so be specific and literal about materials rather than general
about the scene.

Blur is part of the photo: out-of-focus areas stay just as soft, and only what is already sharp gains
detail. Thin real details that cross blurred areas are content, not blur, however fine: name them and
keep every one. If something is too blurry or small to identify for certain,
describe it as soft shapes and colors - never guess what it might be. Don't redesign anything or add
objects that aren't there.

widgets_values: Stay close to the original photo
